triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter-wide module gated the Section 122 surcharge exemption, the Section 232 aluminum duty and the China/Brazil/forced-labor Section 301 duties on the witness's five exemplar line-identity flags (entry_is_line_a/b/c/e) rather than on the membership each provision actually defines, so the surcharge was zeroed on every Section 301-listed line regardless of origin (against the heading's own exclusion-list and 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper' exceptions) while the Brazil and forced-labor duties fell on every line not flagged a or b.
triage.triage_notes: Identical substantive pattern across all 12 indices in this chunk (ch61-ch72); each diff read individually. Two corrections ride together: (1) the named exemplar-coupling/scope defect (chosen kind), and (2) a genuinely missing duty — the new section_232_steel_component_rate + 50% heading-rate parameter wired into schedule_statutory_stack, which on its own would read as unrepresented_clause ('gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had'; PR says it carries 3.89pp). Kind label is contestable: untraceable_branch is defensible too, since entry_is_line_* conditions have no statutory basis and the fix re-grounds them; I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the PR states the harm as the wrong population of lines/origins being suppressed. Decoupling is partial and deliberate: entry_is_line_a/b survive in entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded / entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded and in the Brazil IEEPA term 'if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b', and entry_is_line_d is retained for the beer/Section 338 slot and one China-301 list-1 slot ('Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists'). The section_201_component_rate rename (entry_is_line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv) is a runtime no-op: both branches return 0. Provenance doubt worth a reviewer's eye: the merged file still carries a double-nested metadata.proof.proof.atoms on section_232_steel_component_rate (ch61 line ~3376) and 9903.81.87/.88 are absent from module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths, although the PR's own comment claims 'steel atoms unwrapped to canonical metadata.proof.atoms' and the cited provision 'added to every module's source-verification set'. Step 4 source read was inconclusive: resolve_provision for us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 returned 'unresolved' across all releases, and chapter-99/page-221 and /page-230 in the pinned release are a different HTS vintage that does not contain the cited Section 122 exception text; classification therefore rests on the diff, the module's own proof atoms (versions[1] 'exception' atom quoting 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04', which is exactly what entry_is_section_232_covered now encodes), and the PR body. Serialization dialect group A (from/effective_to, 31 redundant paren pairs). No later commit touches this file.
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempt fails on the fidelity question: the §122 rule's own proof atoms are unchanged by this commit and cite membership-defined exceptions ("subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03", "7202.11.10", "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper ... provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"), while the pre-fix formula gated the zero on entry_is_line_a/entry_is_line_b — identifiers that name the hand-built witness's five exemplar lines and appear nowhere in the cited HTS text, so the encoded condition disagreed with the cited source in a chapter-61 (knitted apparel) instance under either reading of what entry preparation supplies. Where I do dissent is the kind: nothing about the entity (CustomsEntry), period, chapter scope, or output surface was wrong or changed; what was wrong is that every component gate rested on a fixture-identity flag with no grounding in the provision it implements, and the fix re-grounds each one on the membership its own provision defines (§122 exempt/§232 covered, entry_is_section_232_aluminum, china_301_list123/list4a/2024_action/solar, entry_is_section_201_cspv). That is the taxonomy's untraceable_branch ("a branch, condition, or value with no basis in the cited source ... the fix removes or re-grounds it"), with the wrong incidence population being the consequence rather than the defect itself.

triage.verifier_notes: Kind call is a near tie — wrong_entity_or_scope is defensible if "population" is read as "the set of entries a branch fires on"; I prefer untraceable_branch because the ungrounded identifier, not the rule's scope, is what the fix replaces, and the taxonomy reserves "re-grounds it" for exactly this. The diff is not single-kind: (a) brazil_section_301_component_rate and forced_labor_section_301_component_rate additionally ADD a missing list-membership condition the source requires (pre-fix applied the Brazil §301 duty to every Brazil-origin ch61 entry except exemplar lines a/b, with no listed-article gate) — that sub-change reads as unrepresented_clause; (b) the §201 edit is meaning-neutral (`if entry_is_line_e: 0 else: 0` → `if entry_is_section_201_cspv: 0 else: 0`, both branches 0); (c) the new ch61_s232_steel_heading_rate / section_232_steel_component_rate and its stack term are additive coverage the module never claimed (PR: "gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had"), so on their own they would be enhancement, not defect. Exemplar coupling survives this fix elsewhere in the same post-fix file — entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded is still `formula: entry_is_line_a`, entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded still `entry_is_line_b`, and the IEEPA stack still carries `if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b` — so the module remains partly exemplar-gated; if the corpus dedups by defect, note this is one of 100 byte-identical generated chapter instances in commit a9562cfd44 (module index 60 of 100). Source check caveat: resolve_provision for us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-230 against the pinned release returns Rev. 3 steel-TRQ note text, not the aluminum/steel/copper §122 carve-out the atom quotes (page numbering shifts between HTS revisions), so I relied on the module's own unchanged exception atoms rather than a resolved page.
